freeze_procedure_defect_found_before_ope: The first hash recorded (859a08db...) did not round-trip: integer keys in predicted_curve sort numerically in memory and lexicographically after a JSON reload, so the two serialisations differed. Found before any evidence existed and re-issued by hashing the JSON round-trip. The rule it establishes: a frozen prediction whose hash cannot be re-verified FROM DISK is not frozen.

why_the_model_missed: The model is accurate where overheads are small relative to compute (1.0% error at batch 128,
11.5% at 256) and badly wrong where they dominate (55% at batch 16). It systematically
OVER-charged compaction at small batch: it assumed one compaction per iteration at which any row
halts, modelled as min(n-1, E[max]-1), giving 15 compactions at batch 16 against 10 measured,
and it used a c_compact of 87.33 us measured on a synthetic gather of all six state tensors
including the large keys tensor, which over-states the marginal cost inside the loop.
The consequence is that it placed the crossover at 45 when the true crossover is under 16.
consequence: Kill condition applies: the cost model does not locate the crossover, so NO predictive runtime
equation is claimed. The measured curve is reported as an observation.
